Apple has made a bold claim about the Apple Watch Series 12 and Apple Watch Ultra 4. Apple says that the new Health Sensing System on both watches "delivers the most accurate heart rate sensing of any wearable." Apple backs this up with a new study showing how the Series 12's heart rate sensing compares to other leading wearables, including smart rings and fitness bands.

The Health Sensing System is a major upgrade for Apple Watch

The major upgrade in the Apple Watch Series 12 and Apple Watch Ultra 4 comes from the Health Sensing System that drives a number of health and fitness features.

Apple explains: "With the launch of Apple Watch Series 12 and Apple Watch Ultra 4, Apple introduces the Health Sensing System, which includes updated electrical and optical (photoplethysmography, or PPG) heart rate sensors and associated signal-processing algorithms, enabled by new technologies for capabilities such as Recovery HRV and the Readiness app."

How Apple tested the Series 12

According to Apple's nine-page study, testing was conducted between July and August 2026 across five sites in the U.S. and Malaysia. Apple recruited 1,460 adults, of which 1,254 provided at least one set of paired measurements for the final analysis.

Participants wore the Apple Watch Series 12 on one wrist and a competing wrist-worn device on the other, with a Polar H10 ECG chest strap used as the reference standard.

Apple compared the Series 12 against the Garmin Forerunner 970, Google Pixel Watch 4, Huawei Watch 5, Samsung Galaxy Watch 8, and WHOOP 5. Participants also wore an Oura Ring 5 on their index finger, following Oura's instructions.

Testing covered outdoor running, treadmill intervals, cycling, HIIT, and weight training. Apple also measured background heart rate during everyday activities, including rest, desk work, and meal prep while walking.

These scenarios included challenges such as rapid wrist movement, heart rate variability, and "cadence lock," where an optical sensor might mistake a running cadence for a pulse.

What Apple found

Apple says the Series 12 was statistically more accurate than all compared devices overall, in both exercise and everyday scenarios. Out of 159 individual activity-and-measurement comparisons, the Apple Watch achieved statistically better accuracy in 139.

You can read the full study here.

Apple Watch Series 12 is now available to pre-order starting at $399. Apple Watch Ultra 4 is now available to pre-order starting at $799. Both models will go on sale on September 18, one week from now.
